summary.text: 水 is a pictograph of flowing water, drawn as a winding current with marks for droplets. Its common meaning is “water.”

formation.text: The graph depicts a current with droplets beside it; its parts form one picture rather than separate character elements. The Han-era account adds a cosmological explanation, which is a historical interpretation rather than the graphic construction.

components.text: The whole graph pictures flowing water: the central stroke represents the current, and the side marks represent droplets. Early forms vary in the number and arrangement of those marks.

history.text: Oracle forms vary in their side marks, while bronze and Warring States forms are described as retaining the flowing-water picture. These forms show the motif across script traditions without establishing a step-by-step sequence of changes.
The Han-era explanation glosses 水 as “level” and relates it to the cosmology of its time. This is a historical account of the character, distinct from its pictorial construction.

uncertainties.text: Proposals for the spoken word’s earlier pronunciation and its possible relations to words in other languages differ; they concern the word’s history, not a sound component in the graph.

senses.period: Shang oracle-bone examples; individual dates unresolved
senses.text: Reported Shang oracle-bone examples use 水 for water or flooding. The examples are not individually dated, so their relative order is unresolved.
The common current meaning is “water.” Other recorded glosses include liquid, lotion, and juice, but their chronology is not established here.

A bronze inscription is reported to use 水 to write the different word 乞, “request.” This proposed borrowing reuses the sign because the words may have sounded alike or similarly; water did not develop the meaning “request.” The historical sound match is unconfirmed.
One reported oracle-bone use is read as a verb involving either leveling ground with water or washing a temple. Its reading and any connection to the noun “water” remain unresolved.

developments.text: The graph is reported to have been reused for 乞, “request,” on the proposed basis that the words sounded alike or similarly. The old spoken name of the pictured water and a historical comparison of the words’ pronunciations are not established.

limitations.text: The oracle examples are not individually dated. Whether the disputed verbal use is related to the noun “water” remains unresolved.
The proposed sound-based explanation for writing 乞 with 水 lacks a confirmed historical comparison of their pronunciations.
水準 is reported in compounds for a leveling instrument and, later, an abstract “standard” or “level.” These compound meanings are not separate senses of 水, and their stages are undated here.

overview.text: 水 pictures flowing water: a winding current with marks for droplets. Its common meaning is “water.”

components.text: Together, the central line and side marks picture a current and its droplets.
